questionText: [Set 26.1] Under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, the Right to Life and Personal Liberty was expanded by the Supreme Court in the landmark Justice K.S. Puttaswamy judgment (2017) to explicitly include:

options.text: The Right to Strike without notice
The Right to Privacy as an intrinsic fundamental right
The Right to Bear Arms without licensing
The Right to Foreign Dual Citizenship

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 General-Test (General Knowledge & Static Awareness - Indian Constitution Fundamental Rights):
In the historic 9-judge bench ruling in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017), the Supreme Court held unanimously that the Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 26.2] The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of India, responsible for fixing the benchmark policy repo rate, consists of:

options.text: 6 members (3 from RBI including the Governor who holds casting vote, and 3 appointed by Central Government)
12 members appointed exclusively by commercial private banks
5 Supreme Court judges and the Union Finance Minister
3 members all appointed by the World Bank

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 General-Test (General Knowledge & Static Awareness - Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) Composition):
Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act 1934, the MPC comprises 6 members: RBI Governor (Chairperson), Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one RBI officer, and three external experts appointed by the Central Government.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 26.3] An article is sold for Rs. 1200 at a gain of 20%. If it had been sold for Rs. 850, what would have been the percentage loss?

options.text: None of the above criteria are satisfied

questionText: [Set 26.4] A can complete a piece of work in 12 days and B can complete the same work in 24 days. Working together, in how many days can they complete the work?
detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 General-Test (Quantitative Aptitude - Time and Work Combined Rate):
A's one day work = 1/12. B's one day work = 1/24. Combined one day work = 1/12 + 1/24 = (2 + 1) / 24 = 3/24 = 1/8. Total time taken working together = 8 days.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 26.6] Pointing to a photograph of a man, Neha said: 'His mother is the only daughter of my maternal grandfather.' How is Neha related to the man in the photograph?

Neha's maternal grandfather's only daughter is Neha's own mother. Therefore, the man's mother is Neha's mother. This makes the man Neha's brother, and Neha is the man's sister.

questionText: [Set 26.7] In a certain code language, if 'SYSTEM' is coded as 'SYSMET' and 'NEARER' is coded as 'AENRER', how will 'FRACTION' be coded?
detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 General-Test (Logical & Analytical Reasoning - Coding-Decoding Substitution):
The word is divided into two equal halves. In 'SYSTEM' (6 letters): first half 'SYS' reversed is 'SYS'; second half 'TEM' reversed is 'MET' -> 'SYSMET'. In 'FRACTION' (8 letters): first half 'FRAC' reversed is 'CARF'; second half 'TION' reversed is 'NOIT'. Combined: 'CARFNOIT'.

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText:
[Set 26.8] Statements:
1. All roses are flowers.
2. Some flowers are red.

Conclusions:
I. Some roses are red.
II. Some red items are flowers.

Which conclusion(s) logically follow?

options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 General-Test (Logical & Analytical Reasoning - Syllogism Deductive Logic):
From statement 2 'Some flowers are red', by conversion we get 'Some red items are flowers' (Conclusion II is valid). The middle term 'flowers' is undistributed in both premises, so no definite relation can be drawn between 'roses' and 'red' (Conclusion I is not necessarily true).

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 26.43] An article is sold for Rs. 6000 at a gain of 20%. If it had been sold for Rs. 4750, what would have been the percentage loss?
detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 General-Test (Quantitative Aptitude - Profit and Loss Percentage):
Cost Price (CP) = SP * 100 / (100 + Gain%) = 6000 * 100 / 120 = Rs. 5000. If sold at Rs. 4750: Loss = CP - SP = 5000 - 4750 = Rs. 250. Loss % = (250 / 5000) * 100 = 5%.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.
